headline: Sunny, dry and milder than normal through Saturday, then a coastal storm looks increasingly likely to bring a wind-driven soaking rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning, though its exact track and strength are still uncertain.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Strong high pressure keeps New York City and the surrounding area mostly sunny and dry through Wednesday evening, with no watches or advisories in effect. Winds are light, about 6–9 mph from the northwest to west-southwest this afternoon, dropping to 5 mph or less tonight and going calm in many areas outside the city. With clear skies and calm air, outlying spots will cool off more than the city and coast, and patchy freezing fog is likely tonight in river valleys, sheltered inland spots and the Long Island Pine Barrens.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thursday through Saturday stay mostly sunny and dry, with highs several degrees above normal in the upper 50s to mid 60s; a weak disturbance passing Thursday night into Friday morning won't change that much. Overnight lows gradually rise to a few to several degrees above normal, especially in the city and right along the coast. Patchy freezing fog is likely again Thursday night in valleys, sheltered inland areas and the Pine Barrens, with a small chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A low pressure system forming off the Southeast coast this weekend (the National Hurricane Center gives it a 40% chance of becoming tropical or subtropical) is expected to move north to near Cape Hatteras Sunday morning and then over or near the area late Sunday into Monday morning. If it tracks close to the coast, expect a wind-driven soaking rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning: there is a 30–50% chance of 1 inch or more in 24 hours, a 20–30% chance of 2 inches or more, and under a 10% chance of 3–4 inches, with a low, localized risk of flash flooding. A close track could also bring sustained winds of 20–30 mph with gusts of 35–40 mph, while a track farther southeast would limit wind impacts. Drier weather with temperatures near normal is likely later Monday into early next week.

coast: Calm boating conditions through Sunday morning with no advisories: winds mostly from the northwest to west under 15 knots (about 17 mph) and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 feet. Small Craft Advisory or possibly gale conditions could develop later Sunday into Monday depending on the storm's track and strength; the chance of tropical-storm-force winds (39 mph or more sustained) is below 20% and mainly over the ocean southeast of Long Island. Minor coastal flooding is possible early next week with the approaching new moon raising tides, and would be more likely if the storm tracks over or west of the area (currently a low chance).
watch_for: The track and strength of the Sunday–Monday coastal storm: a closer track means heavier rain (1–2+ inches), 35–40 mph gusts and coastal flooding; a track farther offshore means much less.
Whether the storm off the Southeast coast becomes tropical or subtropical this weekend — check National Hurricane Center updates.
Patchy freezing fog tonight and Thursday night, with a small chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses in outlying areas.
confidence: High confidence in dry, mild weather through Saturday; growing confidence that a coastal storm affects the area Sunday into Monday, but low confidence in its exact track, rain totals, winds and coastal impacts.
